summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: almost every Hindi video gets 150 to 1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly stays under 60 views. The best videos explain a familiar gadget with a surprising 'it doesn't do X, it actually does Y' twist, and the strongest ones are robots and clap switches. Videos about everyday gadgets like doors, taps and street lights, plus the YouTube-only uploads, got almost no reach or engagement, and the English video did not catch on either.
winningPattern: Maker-favorite subjects (robots, Arduino modules, clap switch, gyro, IR, mic, DHT11) with a 'X doesn't do the obvious thing, it does this instead' hook in Hinglish, written as a statement or bold claim rather than a 'Kaise...? 🤔' question. Best on Instagram Reels, where they get 1,000+ views and the highest saves and likes. Shares spike on 'myth-busting' sensor facts (UV sunburn, soil sensor) even with low views, so surprising claims travel. Early robot and clap-switch videos on YouTube (400 to 680 views) show those topics also work there.
doMore: Post every video on Instagram as well as YouTube; all the YouTube-only uploads flopped
Make robot and Arduino module videos (gyro, line follower, IR, clap switch) the core of the channel
Use the 'sensor doesn't do X, only does Y' statement hook with a visible failure or demo in the first second
Add a save-worthy or share-worthy payoff such as a wiring tip, a myth correction or a 'try this at home' test
Re-test the 'Gyro Ke Bina Robot Gir Jaata' and 'Clap Switch' formats with new angles instead of repeating the same video
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔' question titles about everyday gadgets (tap, mall door, street light, smoke detector)
Publishing to one platform only, or making near-duplicate videos on the same sensor (clap switch and DHT11 repeats lose reach)
Switching to English narration until Hindi is fully tapped out
